title: Activation profile telemetry and canary rollout for INT8 compatibility
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Objective: build an activation-aware INT8 deployment path that pairs an offline calibration service with lightweight runtime telemetry and a controlled canary rollout. Deliverables: (1) calibration artifact format (per-layer/per-channel scale maps + coverage metadata), (2) a telemetry agent that emits activation histograms and reduced statistics at shard granularity, (3) a canary rollout orchestration flow in the control plane that gates model promotion using automated accuracy checks and runtime SLO signals, and (4) small runtime kernel shims that support signed-8 kernels with per-channel scales and a fast FP16 fallback path.

Scope notes: this ticket focuses on the integration surface and safety automation rather than inventing new quant algorithms. Calibration will consume profiles generated by the existing offline harness; runtime will collect lightweight stats (amax, mean_abs, overflow_count, sample_count) rather than raw tensors. Canary checks will combine offline eval metrics (perplexity/logprob delta, BERTScore) and online telemetry (token latency P95, error rates, generation length drift).

Success criteria: (a) calibration artifact format finalised and stored with model bundles, (b) runtime emits telemetry for >95% of dedicated inference nodes without exceeding 0.5% token latency overhead, (c) canary run automation can detect >1.0% regression in primary eval metric or >20% increase in error rate and automatically rollback, (d) two internal models deployed through the new path with no manual intervention and passing pilot audit.

test_plan: Offline: run calibration harness on calibration corpora (web-text-subset + customer-sim prompts) and produce artifact; verify statistics coverage >= 99% of active channels.
Offline eval: compute baseline and quantized model metrics (perplexity, logprob-delta, BERTScore) on gold eval set; require <=1.0% relative regression unless model-specific waiver granted.
Staging canary: deploy quantized model to 5% traffic cohort; collect runtime telemetry for 24h and run automated quality scripts comparing online generation samples to baseline.
Promote to 25% if no regression; monitor for 72h then promote to 100% with gradual ramp and daily automated checks.
Rollback criteria: automated trigger on metric regression, or manual rollback during incident triage.
migration_steps: Publish calibration artifact format to model registry; update packager to include artifact with model bundle.
Deploy telemetry agent update to dedicated nodes behind feature flag; verify reduced-stat emission to metrics pipeline.
Enable canary orchestration in control plane for a single pilot model and observe behaviour for two weeks before scaling to more models.
Roll out runtime kernel shims with CI gating; include binary compatibility tests against previous kernels.
rollout_strategy: Phase 0: internal-only test on 1 dedicated shard with synthetic traffic
Phase 1: 5% canary for non-critical models for 24-72h
Phase 2: 25% canary for critical internal models for 72h
Phase 3: 100% gradual promotion if all checks pass for 7 days
kernel_changes: Introduce lightweight per-channel scale lookup in matmul microkernel (compatible with existing packed weight layout)
Add a fast-path for zeroed scale vectors to avoid per-channel branching for predominantly FP16-compatible layers
Expose runtime flag to force FP16 fallback for particular ops when overflow_count exceeds threshold
ABI-stable shim layer to allow rolling upgrade of kernels without requiring a full binary rebuild
fallback_policy: Soft-fallback: for transient saturation events, apply per-request FP16 fallback for affected tensors and mark telemetry for follow-up
Hard-fallback: for sustained quality regression (>1.0% eval delta or >20% error-rate increase) trigger canary rollback and redeploy previous model variant
Operator override: SRE/owners can manually pin model to FP16/INT8 via console with immediate effect
acceptance_criteria: Calibration artifacts are produced and validated by harness; schemas committed and documented
Telemetry agent runs on >=95% of dedicated nodes and latency overhead measured and acceptable
Canary automation performs automated promote/rollback based on defined thresholds and integrates with incident runbook
Two pilot models have completed full canary workflow and remained within quality bounds for 7 days
